title: Platform systems & services — runbooks, dashboards, alerts, and roadmap (Q2 2027)
author: Lena Rodriguez
content:
Overview:

This page is the canonical platform engineering reference for systems and services runbooks, dashboard and alert standards, retrospectives from major incidents, and the Q2 2027 roadmap. It is intended for oncall engineers, platform owners, product and infra partners, and SREs operating Redwood Inference platform services.

Scope:
- Services covered: platform-gateway, metrics-ingest, job-runner, model-orchestrator, secret-store, cluster-controlplane (k8s), storage-proxy.
- Topics: runbooks (P0/P1/P2 playbooks), dashboard templates, alert rules and thresholds, runbook change process, recent retrospectives, and upcoming roadmap items.

Ownership and contacts:
- Platform oncall rotation: platform-oncall@redwood.com (primary)
- Pager escalation: platform-paging Slack channel -> oncall -> platform-eng-manager (escalation window 15m).
- Service owners (primary):
  - platform-gateway: @marcus (Marcus Lee)
  - metrics-ingest: @asha (Asha Nair)
  - job-runner: @lena (Lena Rodriguez)
  - secret-store: @ryan (Ryan Kim)

Service-level objectives (SLOs) and indicators (SLIs):
- platform-gateway: availability 99.95% monthly, request p99 latency < 120ms for 512B payloads.
- metrics-ingest: availability 99.9% monthly, ingestion success rate >= 99.5% (5m rolling).
- job-runner: job-completion 95% within target execution window, queue length < 500.

Key dashboards (templates):
- Platform Overview (team-level) — KPI row: availability, error-rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, cost-per-token estimate.
- Service Detail (per-service) — request rate, success rate, latency heatmap, CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth.
- Jobs & Backfills — outstanding jobs, retry rate, average duration.
- Secrets & Config — KMS error rates, rotator success, dead-letter counts.

Dashboard template (recommended panels):
| Panel | Metric | Alert tie-in | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Availability | availability_pct (5m) | P1 if < 99.9% for 10m | service-owner |
| Error rate | errors / total_requests (5m) | P1 if > 0.5% for 5m | service-owner |
| p99 latency | latency_p99 (5m) | P2 if > target_threshold for 10m | service-owner |

Alerting standards and thresholds:
- Severity mapping:
  - P0 (SEV0): Total outage (all regions) or data-loss. Pager immediate, cross-team warroom.
  - P1 (SEV1): Service-level outage or major degradation (SLO burn rate > 10x for 30m). Pager, follow incident process.
  - P2 (SEV2): Functional degradation impacting a subset of customers (sustained errors or latency). Email + oncall Slack.

- Example alert rules (Grafana / Prometheus alert syntax summarized):
  1) platform_gw_5xx_rate_high: IF rate(http_requests_total{job="platform-gateway",status=~"5.."}[5m]) / rate(http_requests_total{job="platform-gateway"}[5m]) > 0.005 THEN P1 after 5m.
  2) metrics_ingest_latency_spike: IF histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(metrics_ingest_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) > 2s THEN P2 after 10m.
  3) job_runner_queue_growth: IF increase(job_queue_length[10m]) > 200 THEN P1.

Alert routing and runbooks:
- All P0/P1 alerts: page platform-oncall and create an incident in the incident tracker with link to relevant runbook.
- Runbook link must be included in the alert annotation (runbook_url).
- If oncall cannot mitigate within 15 minutes, escalate to platform-eng-manager and open a warroom channel.

Primary runbooks (short summaries; full runbooks linked):
1) platform-gateway-p1-runbook (link: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/platform-gateway-p1):
   - Symptoms: 5xx spike across routes, p99 latency > 500ms, increased queue length on API-frontend.
   - Immediate checks: service health, downstream dependency errors, recent deploys (git commit/tag).
   - Mitigations (ordered): 1) roll back last deploy if correlated; 2) increase replica count to shed backlog; 3) enable degraded-mode config to bypass costly plugin; 4) route traffic to dedicated capacity pool.
   - Recovery verification: p99 back within target for 15m, error rate returned to baseline.

2) metrics-ingest-p1-runbook (link: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/metrics-ingest-p1):
   - Symptoms: ingestion backlog growth, consumer lag > 10 minutes, high write error rate to storage-proxy.
   - Immediate checks: storage-proxy health, k8s pod restarts, Kafka / queue broker lag, disk pressure on storage.
   - Mitigations: 1) scale consumers; 2) apply backpressure (throttle producers) using ingress rate limiters; 3) failover to warm storage-proxy replica.

3) job-runner-p1-runbook (link: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/job-runner-p1):
   - Symptoms: job queue growth, high retry rates, stuck workers.
   - Immediate checks: worker health, queue length metrics, recent config changes.
   - Mitigations: 1) drain and restart workers with controlled concurrency; 2) run targeted cleanup for poison messages; 3) temporarily increase worker pool on Dedicated.

Runbook change and review process:
1) Author opens a PR on the runbook repo (docs/runbooks/*.md).
2) At least one service owner and one oncall reviewer must approve.
3) Changes tagged with semver and referenced in the alert annotation examples.
4) Major runbook changes (behavior changes, new mitigations) must be announced on platform-all and during next oncall handoff.

Retrospective highlights (recent incidents):
- Incident: platform-gateway latency spike (2026-10-21) — root cause: a degraded kernel-level networking config on new node image.
  - Impact: 30m of elevated p99 (up to 900ms) for hosted API routes, 3% increase in error rates.
  - Actions taken: rollback node image, added pre-prod soak for node images, added sysctl check into node-bootstrap.
  - Follow-ups: automated canary fleet for node images (owner: eng-infra), SLO alert tuning for faster detection.

- Incident: metrics-ingest backlog (2026-12-08) — root cause: storage-proxy GC throttle after config change.
  - Impact: 4h ingestion delay, delayed cost analytics.
  - Actions: emergency failover to cold-storage replica, revert GC config change, implement config guardrails.
  - Follow-ups: pre-deploy integration test for storage-proxy (owner: eng-platform).

Roadmap (Q2 2027 priorities):
- Monitoring & alerts:
  - Migrate critical dashboards to unified Grafana folder and standardize dashboard JSON schema (owner: observability team).
  - Implement anomaly-detection baseline for p99 latency using historical models (MVP).
- Runbooks & automation:
  - Convert top-10 runbooks to automated remediation playbooks (K8s job + runbook-triggered workflows).
  - Add runbook linting and CI checks to require annotations and test links.
- Reliability & capacity:
  - Capacity planning project for Dedicated pools (predictive autoscaling).
  - Improve prefix/KV caching metrics exposure for model-orchestrator.

How-tos (common procedures):
- How to add a service dashboard:
  1) Duplicate the Service Detail template in Grafana.
  2) Replace datasource and metric filters with your service job label.
  3) Add runbook_url to the dashboard and to top-panel alerts.
  4) Request review from observability team via PR and include reviewer for service-owner.

- How to onboard new oncaller:
  1) Complete platform runbook reading list.
  2) Shadow two rotations with the current oncall.
  3) Verify access to pager duty, slack, incident tracker, and runbook repo.

Postmortem and continuous improvement cadence:
- Major incidents (P0/P1) require a postmortem published within 5 business days and a tracked action in the reliability board.
- Monthly reliability review: review SLO burn, jitter, repeated alert sources, and open action items.

Appendix: useful links and CLI snippets:
- Incident tracker: https://incidents.redwood.local/ (internal)
- Grafana folder: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/platform-team
- Example kubectl commands: kubectl -n platform get pods -o wide; kubectl -n platform logs deploy/platform-gateway --since=15m

If you have questions or need a walk-through of any runbook or dashboard, ping the platform-systems Slack channel or reach out to the owners listed above.
